what_its_for: RYDAPT is used to treat two conditions: (1) Adults with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has a specific gene change called FLT3 mutation — it is used together with chemotherapy. (2) Adults with rare tumors called aggressive systemic mastocytosis (ASM), systemic mastocytosis with associated blood cancer (SM-AHN), or mast cell leukemia (MCL). Your doctor will test your blood or tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Take RYDAPT by mouth with food (a meal or a snack). Swallow the capsules whole — do not open, crush, or chew them. Try to take your doses at the same times each day. If you vomit after taking a dose, do NOT take another dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg (four 25 mg capsules) taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart, with food. For AML patients, this is taken on days 8 through 21 of each cycle of chemotherapy, and then continued after chemotherapy is finished. For mastocytosis patients, it is taken continuously every day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regularly scheduled time. Do not double up or take an extra dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store RYDAPT capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Short trips to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) are okay. Keep the capsules in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from light and moisture. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit, as they can increase the amount of RYDAPT in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Many medicines can interact with RYDAPT, especially antibiotics (like rifampin), antifungals (like ketoconazole), seizure medicines, and St. John's Wort. Do not start or stop any medicines without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Women should not breastfeed while taking RYDAPT and for at least 4 months after the last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you have any of these: fever, chills, or signs of infection; shortness of breath, chest pain, or fast heartbeat; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that you cannot control; skin rash, blistering, or peeling; signs of low blood cell counts such as unusual bruising, bleeding, or extreme tiredness; signs of lung problems such as new or worsening cough or trouble breathing; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or if you think you may be pregnant. Also tell your doctor if you have any side effects that bother you or do not go away.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks to months before you notice the full benefit of RYDAPT. Your doctor will do regular blood tests and check-ups to see how the medicine is working. Do not stop taking RYDAPT without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and birth control: RYDAPT can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Tell your doctor right away if you or your partner become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 4 months after stopping RYDAPT. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Children: RYDAPT is not currently approved for use in patients under 18 years old.
